text:
Alex: Heads-up — ran into a correctness hole in the prefix cache when evicting tombstones. If a writer deletes a prefix then we evict the tombstone before a reader sees the deletion, we can serve stale data.
Maria: Oof. Is this the cross-node handoff case or same-node eviction race?
Alex: Cross-node. Sequence: writer A deletes, writes tombstone with lease epoch E. Tombstone gets GC'd on node X during eviction, reader hits node Y which still has old data in its local cache.
Devon: Hmm. Did the tombstone carry a monotonic version/fence token? We rely on epoch tokens in the handoff usually.
Alex: Right, we have a fence token but eviction currently strips tombstones entirely (to save memory).
Katie: What's the strict invariant we want? Strong read-after-delete for subsequent reads in all nodes? Or eventual consistency is okay for some customers?
Alex: For some paths we need causal read-after-write — after delete returns success, any subsequent read should not return the deleted value if routed anywhere.
Maria: That implies we need global visibility of the deletion before tombstone removal. Two options: (1) delay tombstone eviction until it's been observed by all relevant nodes, or (2) keep a lightweight delete-epoch index that nodes consult on miss/handoff.
Devon: (2) sounds cheaper: keep small per-prefix metadata: last-deleted-epoch. On a cache miss, we check prefix metadata to validate stale entries.
Katie: Tradeoffs: metadata service adds an extra hop on misses and more state. Delay eviction adds memory pressure and hurts cold start.
Alex: Proposed hybrid: keep tombstones locally for short window W, and publish a last-deleted-epoch to the cluster membership stream immediately. Nodes can check the epoch on miss or when seeing a local entry older than epoch.
Maria: That gives low-latency correctness for most cases and limits memory retention. Need to define W and fallback rules. Also consider network partitions.
Devon: What about races where reader sees old entry before it learns about the epoch update? On a miss it will check the metadata and fix, but if it's a hit we still might serve stale value.
Alex: Exactly — so we also need a cheap validation on cache hits: store per-entry "observed_epoch" and if local observed_epoch < cluster_last_deleted_epoch for that prefix, treat as invalid and revalidate. That makes hits slightly heavier but avoids stale serves.
Katie: Can we piggyback epoch checks on existing RPCs (e.g., lease heartbeats or lease-acquire flow) to avoid extra round trips?
Maria: Yes. Add epoch to the lease/handshake response. That way nodes get updated epoch info opportunistically.
Devon: Also consider making strict mode opt-in per-tenant or per-prefix. Enterprise users may want the stronger guarantee, free-tier gets eventual.
Alex: Good call. We'll spec: default eventual with small tombstone window + epoch pub/sub. Opt-in strict mode keeps tombstones until cluster epoch ack from all nodes or uses a consensus write to a small metadata store.
Maria: Tests to add: cross-node delete then immediate read with randomized routing + partition simulation. Measure false-positive stale serves.
Katie: Metrics: tombstone retention bytes, epoch propagation lag, stale-serve counter, revalidate rate.
kv-bot: deploybot: smoke tests queued for prefetcheviction-proto branch — 5 jobs. :robot_face:
Devon: Implementation checklist: (1) add per-prefix last-deleted-epoch in metadata stream, (2) store observed_epoch per cache entry, (3) on hit compare observed_epoch vs cluster epoch, (4) honor opt-in strict policy, (5) expose metrics and e2e tests.
Alex: I'll draft an RFC/patch with pseudo-code for the hit-path validation. Quick sketch:
```
on_cache_hit(entry, prefix):
  cluster_epoch = cache.local_prefix_epoch(prefix) // opportunistic, may be stale
  if entry.observed_epoch < cluster_epoch:
    return revalidate_from_store(prefix)
  else:
    return entry.value
```
Devon: Looks good. Add a fast-path where observed_epoch == 0 (unknown) triggers conservative revalidate for strict mode only.
Maria: Sync with infra: we need to ensure epoch pub/sub scales for many prefixes — probably use batching and bloom-based dissemination for hot prefixes.
Katie: I'll coordinate with infra next week. Alex, can you open the RFC and link the test plan?
Alex: Will do. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
